Package dayplanner

Class Time

java.lang.Object
dayplanner.Time
All Implemented Interfaces:
Comparable<Time>
public class Time extends Object implements Comparable<Time>

Represents an instant in time with minute-level precision. This is not a time-zone-aware instant and has no seconds or daylight-saving rules.

Each component is stored as a plain integer and validated against the following ranges:

  • year: 1–9999
  • month: 1–12
  • day: 1 to the maximum days in the given month (respects leap years for February; see maxDaysInMonth(int year, int month))
  • hour: 0–23
  • minute: 0–59

The string form produced by toString() is YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM, e.g. 2026/09/15 14:30.

There are also static methods for dealing with Time instances.

    • Time

      public Time()
      Constructs a Time initialized to minimum allowed values (0001/01/01 00:00).

    • Time

      public Time(int year, int month, int day, int hour, int minute)

      Constructs a Time with specified components.

      Invalid components are ignored by individual setters, leaving the current or default component unchanged. Use isValidTime(int, int, int, int, int) when all components must be accepted together.

      Parameters:
      year - The year.
      month - The month.
      day - The day.
      hour - The hour.
      minute - The minute.

    • Time

      public Time(String formatString)
      Constructs a Time by parsing a string in YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM format. Invalid components default to their minimum allowed values.
      Parameters:
      formatString - String containing at least five numeric components, such as 2026/09/15 14:30; separators may be slash, colon, comma, or whitespace.

    • toString

      public String toString()

      Returns a string representation of this time in YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM format.

      Month, day, hour, and minute are zero-padded to two digits; year is zero-padded to four. For example, September 5, 2026 at 8:03 AM is formatted as 2026/09/05 08:03.

      Overrides:
      toString in class Object
      Returns:
      Formatted time string.

    • compareTo

      public int compareTo(Time other)

      Compares this time with another time chronologically.

      Fields are compared in order: year, then month, then day, then hour, then minute. The first field that differs determines the result.

      Specified by:
      compareTo in interface Comparable<Time>
      Parameters:
      other - The other time to compare with.
      Returns:
      A negative integer, zero, or a positive integer as this time precedes, equals, or follows other.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - If other is null.
